(There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

---
paths:

---

# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.
- A bug is fixed separately from a refactoring, test first.

## Blueprint seam

- A new Blueprint exposure is opened when needed, not "just in case".
- Logic is not duplicated between an EventGraph and C++: the decision is in C++, the Blueprint only calls.
- Renaming a `UCLASS`/`UPROPERTY`/`UFUNCTION` visible in Blueprints only with CoreRedirects.
- Deletions (C++, assets) only through a dry run with counts and the author's explicit yes.

## Done (end of a task with code)

1. `bash Tools/Build/build_and_test.sh --open` is green: build, `Jam.` tests without failures, checks. The agent
   closes the editor and runs the full build itself, without asking.
2. Every new `check_code.py` warning is fixed or justified in one line of the report.
3. New decisions are covered by `Jam.` tests, their number did not drop.
4. A git commit in English.
=====
# Questions for the author

Things that need Pavlo's eyes. The work does not wait: each question has the default the agent already took.

## Open

### Q1. The name NEON RONIN is taken on Steam (Thu 13:38)

- Checked: Steam app 1929540 is "Neon Ronin" by TYPE-III, a turn-based cyberpunk rogue-lite, status "coming soon"
  (store page read on 12 Nov). An itch search for "neon ronin" showed no game with this exact name.
- A jam entry with the same name is not forbidden, but the win title is the name, and a search for the game will
  land on theirs.
- **Default:** keep NEON RONIN as the working title today; all strings are in one place, a rename is one line.
- Options if you want a free name: NEON RONIN ZERO, LAST RONIN OF NEON, RONIN.EXE, NEON BUSHIDO. Not checked yet;

# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.

- A new Blueprint exposure is opened when needed, not "just in case".

# Tickets

One file per ticket. Status: `todo`, `doing`, `done`, `cut`. A ticket is done when its `Jam.` tests are green in
`build_and_test.sh` and the change is committed.

## Architecture in five lines (decided at the start of block A)

- The fight is a **pure simulation**: `FJamFight` (plain data: two fighters, projectiles, hazards, the mechanic
  ledger, the steal state) advanced by `JamFightRules::Step` at a fixed 60 Hz. No world, no actors, flat arena in 2D.
- Everything a fighter does comes in as an **intent** (`FJamIntent`: move, aim, buttons). The player controller, the
  boss brain and the hero bot all write intents, so the hero and the boss run the same mechanic code.
- A **mechanic** is a sim-side component with an owner; a steal is a change of owner in the ledger.
- Folders: `Core` (types, balance, ini loading), `Sim` (rules and the subsystem that hosts the fight), `Game` (glue:
  game mode, controller, demo run), `View` (arena, fighters, projectiles, cameras), `UI`. `Core` and `Sim` never
  include `View`, `UI`, `Audio`. The game mode owns the frame order: input, simulation, views, camera.
- Balance numbers live in one place: `[JamBalance]` in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`.

## Thursday: the prototype on beans

|---|---|---|---|
| [T-001](T-001_skeleton_balance_fixed_step.md) | A | Skeleton: folders, game mode, arena map, balance data, fixed-step sim driver | done |

| [T-003](T-003_aim.md) | A | Aim abstraction | done |
| [T-004](T-004_three_cameras.md) | A | Three cameras on F1, F2, F3 | done |
| [T-005](T-005_ball_shot.md) | A | The weak ball shot and projectiles | done |
| [T-006](T-006_boss_dummy_health.md) | A | Boss dummy with health, debug HUD | done |
| [T-007](T-007_mechanic_ledger.md) | B | Mechanics with an owner, the ball fallback | done |
| [T-008](T-008_katana.md) | B | Katana | done |
| [T-009](T-009_shuriken.md) | B | Shuriken | done |
| [T-010](T-010_dash.md) | B | Dash | done |
| [T-011](T-011_boss_brain.md) | B | Boss brain: chase, memo volley, telegraphed slam | done |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Autonomous build + automation test cycle for the jam project (ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld tooling).
#   build_and_test.sh [--no-build] [--no-test] [--no-check] [--open] [--filter Jam.]
# Closes this checkout's JamGame editor only (graceful first, forced after 30 s; editors of other worktrees and
# projects stay open),
# runs the full editor build, runs the project's automation tests headless and prints a summary, then the
# Tools pytest suite and the code checks (Tools/Quality/check_code.py, warnings only).
# --open relaunches the editor afterwards; ignored in a linked git worktree.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
PROJ="$ROOT/JamGame.uproject"
LOGDIR="$ROOT/Saved/Logs"
OUT="$ROOT/Saved/BuildCycle"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.
- A bug is fixed separately from a refactoring, test first.

## Blueprint seam

- A new Blueprint exposure is opened when needed, not "just in case".
- Logic is not duplicated between an EventGraph and C++: the decision is in C++, the Blueprint only calls.
- Renaming a `UCLASS`/`UPROPERTY`/`UFUNCTION` visible in Blueprints only with CoreRedirects.
- Deletions (C++, assets) only through a dry run with counts and the author's explicit yes.

## Done (end of a task with code)

1. `bash Tools/Build/build_and_test.sh --open` is green: build, `Jam.` tests without failures, checks. The agent
   closes the editor and runs the full build itself, without asking.
2. Every new `check_code.py` warning is fixed or justified in one line of the report.
3. New decisions are covered by `Jam.` tests, their number did not drop.
4. A git commit in English.

# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.
- A bug is fixed separately from a refactoring, test first.

## Blueprint seam

- A new Blueprint exposure is opened when needed, not "just in case".
- Logic is not duplicated between an EventGraph and C++: the decision is in C++, the Blueprint only calls.
- Renaming a `UCLASS`/`UPROPERTY`/`UFUNCTION` visible in Blueprints only with CoreRedirects.
- Deletions (C++, assets) only through a dry run with counts and the author's explicit yes.

## Done (end of a task with code)

1. `bash Tools/Build/build_and_test.sh --open` is green: build, `Jam.` tests without failures, checks. The agent
   closes the editor and runs the full build itself, without asking.
2. Every new `check_code.py` warning is fixed or justified in one line of the report.
3. New decisions are covered by `Jam.` tests, their number did not drop.
4. A git commit in English.

</system-reminder>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Records a clip of the game playing itself: the bot drives the hero on the top-down camera.
#   demo_clip.sh [seconds] [output.mp4] [camera]
# camera: ignored since T-018 (only the top-down camera is left), kept so older calls still work.
# Opens a game window for the length of the clip plus the start-up: warn the author first.
# The game saves every frame as a PNG at a fixed 30 fps (see Source/JamGame/Public/Game/JamDemo.h), ffmpeg joins them.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
SECONDS_TO_RUN="${1:-26}"
OUT="${2:-$ROOT/Saved/Demo/demo_$(date +%m%d_%H%M).mp4}"
FRAMES="$ROOT/Saved/Demo/frames"
LOG="$ROOT/Saved/Demo/demo.log"
CAMERA="${3:-}"
mkdir -p "$FRAMES" "$(dirname "$OUT")"

# Git Bash would turn /Game/... into a path under its own install folder.
MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL="*" "$UE/Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor.exe" "$ROOT/JamGame.uproject" /Game/Maps/Arena -game -windowed \
	-resx=1280 -resy=720 -nosplash -unattended -JamDemo -JamCapture="$FRAMES" -JamDemoSeconds="$SECONDS_TO_RUN" -abslog="$LOG" \
	${CAMERA:+-JamDemoCamera="$CAMERA"}
echo "[demo] game exit $?"
grep -E "LogJam[A-Za-z]*: (Warning|Error)|Fatal error|Ensure condition failed" "$LOG" | cut -c1-200 | sort | uniq -c | head -12

# Frames of a longer earlier run stay in the folder under higher numbers: the clip takes only this run's frames.
COUNT=$((SECONDS_TO_RUN * 30))
ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -framerate 30 -i "$FRAMES/f_%05d.png" -frames:v "$COUNT" -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 23 "$OUT"
echo "[demo] ffmpeg exit $?"
ls -la "$OUT"

content.content:
def saw(freq, n):
    t = np.arange(n) / RATE
    return 2.0 * ((t * freq) % 1.0) - 1.0


def square(freq, n):
    return np.sign(np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * np.arange(n) / RATE))


def lowpass(x, k):
    """One-pole low pass, k in (0, 1]: smaller is darker. Run over two laps so the loop point has no click."""
    lap = np.concatenate([x, x])
    y = np.empty_like(lap)
    acc = 0.0
    for i, v in enumerate(lap):
        acc += k * (v - acc)
        y[i] = acc
    return y[len(x):]


def chord_at(bar):
    return bar // 2 % 4


def drums():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    kick_n = int(0.25 * RATE)
    t = np.arange(kick_n) / RATE
    kick = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (50 * t + 90 * (1 - np.exp(-t * 30)) / 30)) * np.exp(-t * 12)
    snare_n = int(0.18 * RATE)
    snare = rng.uniform(-1, 1, snare_n) * env(snare_n, 0.001, 0.05) * 0.6
    hat_n = int(0.05 * RATE)
    hat = np.diff(rng.uniform(-1, 1, hat_n + 1)) * env(hat_n, 0.0005, 0.012) * 0.25
    for beat in range(BARS * 4):
        place(track, beat * BEAT, kick)
        if beat % 2 == 1:
            place(track, beat * BEAT, snare)
        place(track, beat * BEAT, hat)
        place(track, (beat + 0.5) * BEAT, hat)
    return track


def bass():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    note_n = int(BEAT / 2 * RATE)
    for eighth in range(BARS * 8):
        root = ROOTS[chord_at(eighth // 8)] - 12
        tone = saw(hz(root), note_n) * env(note_n, 0.005, 0.18)
        place(track, eighth * BEAT / 2, tone * 0.5)
    return lowpass(track, 0.08)


def pad():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    span_n = int(8 * BEAT * RATE)
    shape = np.minimum(1, np.minimum(np.arange(span_n) / (0.6 * RATE), (span_n - np.arange(span_n)) / (0.6 * RATE)))
    for part in range(4):
        tone = sum(saw(hz(n) * d, span_n) for n in CHORDS[part] for d in (0.997, 1.003)) / 6.0
        place(track, part * 8 * BEAT, tone * shape * 0.35)
    return lowpass(track, 0.05)


def lead():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    note_n = int(BEAT / 4 * RATE)
    for sixteenth in range(BARS * 16):
        chord = CHORDS[chord_at(sixteenth // 16)]
        note = chord[ARP[sixteenth % len(ARP)]] + 12
        tone = square(hz(note), note_n) * env(note_n, 0.002, 0.07)
        place(track, sixteenth * BEAT / 4, tone * 0.18)
    return lowpass(track, 0.25)


def poc_loop():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    click_n = int(0.03 * RATE)
    for beat in range(BARS * 4):
        freq = 1760 if beat % 4 == 0 else 880
        place(track, beat * BEAT, np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * np.arange(click_n) / RATE) * env(click_n, 0.0005, 0.008) * 0.5)
    return track


def write(path, mono):
    peak = np.max(np.abs(mono)) or 1.0
    pcm = (np.clip(mono / peak * 0.7, -1, 1) * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    stereo = np.repeat(pcm[:, None], 2, axis=1)
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as out:
        out.setnchannels(2)
        out.setsampwidth(2)
        out.setframerate(RATE)
        out.writeframes(stereo.tobytes())


def main():
    out_dir = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "Audio/Stub")
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stems = {
        "mus_main_1_drums.wav": drums,
        "mus_main_2_bass.wav": bass,
        "mus_main_3_pad.wav": pad,
        "mus_main_4_lead.wav": lead,
        "mus_poc_loop.wav": poc_loop,
    }
    for name, make in stems.items():
        write(out_dir / name, make())

def saw(freq, n):
    t = np.arange(n) / RATE
    return 2.0 * ((t * freq) % 1.0) - 1.0


def square(freq, n):
    return np.sign(np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * np.arange(n) / RATE))


def lowpass(x, k):
    """One-pole low pass, k in (0, 1]: smaller is darker. Run over two laps so the loop point has no click."""
    lap = np.concatenate([x, x])
    y = np.empty_like(lap)
    acc = 0.0
    for i, v in enumerate(lap):
        acc += k * (v - acc)
        y[i] = acc
    return y[len(x):]


def chord_at(bar):
    return bar // 2 % 4


def drums():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    kick_n = int(0.25 * RATE)
    t = np.arange(kick_n) / RATE
    kick = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (50 * t + 90 * (1 - np.exp(-t * 30)) / 30)) * np.exp(-t * 12)
    snare_n = int(0.18 * RATE)
    snare = rng.uniform(-1, 1, snare_n) * env(snare_n, 0.001, 0.05) * 0.6
    hat_n = int(0.05 * RATE)
    hat = np.diff(rng.uniform(-1, 1, hat_n + 1)) * env(hat_n, 0.0005, 0.012) * 0.25
    for beat in range(BARS * 4):
        place(track, beat * BEAT, kick)
        if beat % 2 == 1:
            place(track, beat * BEAT, snare)
        place(track, beat * BEAT, hat)
        place(track, (beat + 0.5) * BEAT, hat)
    return track


def bass():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    note_n = int(BEAT / 2 * RATE)
    for eighth in range(BARS * 8):
        root = ROOTS[chord_at(eighth // 8)] - 12
        tone = saw(hz(root), note_n) * env(note_n, 0.005, 0.18)
        place(track, eighth * BEAT / 2, tone * 0.5)
    return lowpass(track, 0.08)


def pad():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    span_n = int(8 * BEAT * RATE)
    shape = np.minimum(1, np.minimum(np.arange(span_n) / (0.6 * RATE), (span_n - np.arange(span_n)) / (0.6 * RATE)))
    for part in range(4):
        tone = sum(saw(hz(n) * d, span_n) for n in CHORDS[part] for d in (0.997, 1.003)) / 6.0
        place(track, part * 8 * BEAT, tone * shape * 0.35)
    return lowpass(track, 0.05)


def lead():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    note_n = int(BEAT / 4 * RATE)
    for sixteenth in range(BARS * 16):
        chord = CHORDS[chord_at(sixteenth // 16)]
        note = chord[ARP[sixteenth % len(ARP)]] + 12
        tone = square(hz(note), note_n) * env(note_n, 0.002, 0.07)
        place(track, sixteenth * BEAT / 4, tone * 0.18)
    return lowpass(track, 0.25)


def poc_loop():
    track = np.zeros(N)
    click_n = int(0.03 * RATE)
    for beat in range(BARS * 4):
        freq = 1760 if beat % 4 == 0 else 880
        place(track, beat * BEAT, np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * np.arange(click_n) / RATE) * env(click_n, 0.0005, 0.008) * 0.5)
    return track


def write(path, mono):
    peak = np.max(np.abs(mono)) or 1.0
    pcm = (np.clip(mono / peak * 0.7, -1, 1) * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    stereo = np.repeat(pcm[:, None], 2, axis=1)
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as out:
        out.setnchannels(2)
        out.setsampwidth(2)
        out.setframerate(RATE)
        out.writeframes(stereo.tobytes())


def main():
    out_dir = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "Audio/Stub")
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stems = {
        "mus_main_1_drums.wav": drums,
        "mus_main_2_bass.wav": bass,
        "mus_main_3_pad.wav": pad,
        "mus_main_4_lead.wav": lead,
        "mus_poc_loop.wav": poc_loop,
    }
    for name, make in stems.items():
        write(out_dir / name, make())
        print(f"[stems] {out_dir / name}  {LENGTH:.1f} s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# T-022 The finisher with the Ultimate

**Block:** D · **Status:** done

## Goal

The end of the road: at zero the Publisher is stunned, everything returns at once (mechanics, layers, music), the
hero's meter is full, and only the Ultimate lands the final blow.

## Scope

- The stun (`JamOutcomeRules`, built in T-015) also fills the hero's meter.
- The win needs the final blow: a hit reported with `JamUltimateRules::SlashId`. A katana or ball hit on the stunned
  boss is a hit, fills the meter, and ends nothing; a slash that misses can be earned again that way.
- The stun card reads `E: the Ultimate lands the final blow.`

## Test seam

`Jam.Outcome.TheStunFillsTheMeter` (new), `Jam.Outcome.TheUltimateLandsTheFinalBlow` (was
`AHitOnTheStunnedBossWins`: the katana now hits without winning), `Jam.Outcome.EveryCutComesBeforeTheStun` (the hero
also presses E). Red first: 2 failing.

## Done

128 `Jam.` tests green, 0 code check warnings. Bot: 60 of 60. Clip of a whole fight down to the bean and back:
`Clips/t022_road_down_and_back.mp4`. Shipping package of block D.

# T-029 Readable attacks: hit feedback, camera shake, the explosive in his hands

**Block:** G · **Status:** done (on stand-ins; the real VFX come with T-027 and the art)

## Goal

A person, not only the bot, can read the fight from the top-down camera: what hits and how hard, when the parry
window closes, and which of the Publisher's shuriken will blow up (the finding of T-033).

## Scope

- `JamFeedbackRules` (`View`, pure), numbers in `[JamFeedback]` of `DefaultGame.ini`:
  - `ShakeKick`: the slam, the Ultimate slash, an explosion and the hero hurt shake the camera; swings, dashes and
    hits on the boss do not. `ShakeLeft` dies out squared over `ShakeSeconds`, `ShakeOffset` never leaves the
    amplitude. The rig keeps the stronger of a running shake and a new kick.
  - `ShowsBlastRing`: an explosive shuriken of the Publisher's carries a dashed ring of its blast radius on the
    ground; the hero's own, or one he parried back, does not.
  - `SparkRadius`: a ring around the body that was hit, sized by the damage between two limits.
  - `FlashWeight`: the hurt hero flashes fully white; the Publisher only by the size of the blow (a ball tints him,
    the katana finisher flashes him): "the boss flashes white a lot" is gone.
  - `ParryRingScale`: the parry ring opens wide and closes with the window, so the time left is seen.
- Views: the explosive shuriken is yellow and pulses (orange was too close to his red); the parry ring is brighter.
  The spark of a hit on the Publisher goes with the hero's effects layer when it is cut.

## Test seam

`Jam.Feedback.OnlyHeavyBlowsShakeTheCamera`, `ShakeDiesOut`, `TheBossExplosiveShowsItsBlast`,
`HitsShowTheirWeight`, `ParryRingClosesWithTheWindow`, `IniIsComplete`. Red first: 6 failing with stub rules.

## Done

134 `Jam.` tests green, 0 code check warnings. Clip `Clips/t029_readability.mp4` (30 s, bot): sparks on hits, the
yellow explosive. The blast ring needs a stolen shuriken and shows in the whole-fight clip of the session.

Written Fri 13 Nov 23:59 PC clock (UTC+2) at the end of the first jam session. The next session starts from the
prompt at the bottom of this file.

## Where we are

- **Last commit:** `3d5b8ac`. Tag `k1` is on `136fe26`, the commit the K1 Shipping package was built from. The
  working tree was clean before this file.
- **Nothing was built after Thu 16:05.** The session stood still for all of Friday. Blocks D and E are not started
  and checkpoint K2 (test build, Fri 18:00) was missed. The plan is one working day behind.
- **What is left on the clock:** feature freeze Sat 22:00, video Sun 18:00, submit Sun 20:00 and never later than
  21:59.

## What the game does today (107 `Jam.` tests green, code check without warnings)

- The whole fight on beans: move, aim, ball, katana, shuriken, dash; the Publisher chases, throws a memo volley
  that leads its target and slams with a warning circle.
- Three steals at 75, 50 and 25 percent with the choice card; he uses what he stole; stun at zero, everything
  returns, the last blow; both titles; retry from the last steal.
- A hero bot plays whole fights. On the numbers of the game it wins 60 of 60 in all six steal orders, median
  167 seconds (126 to 176), closest win 5 of 100 health.
- Shipping package of `136fe26`: `Saved/Packaged/NeonRonin_K1.zip` (303 MB) and
  `Saved/Packaged/Windows/JamGame.exe`. Smoke-run with the bot, fine.

## Decisions made by the author

- **Camera: 0, top-down 3/4** (answered Fri 13 Nov). T-018 is unblocked: keep it, switch the other two off. Hero
  animations can be ordered for a top-down view.

## Still waiting on people (defaults are taken, see `QUESTIONS.md`)

- Q4 the itch draft page address (account `Pavyny`). Without it there is no `butler push`, and the zip is over the
  30 MB limit of the file channel, so **no build has reached the author yet**. T-017 stays `doing` for this reason.
- Q1 the name (NEON RONIN is taken on Steam; default: keep it). Q2 concepts (default hero A, boss A; no model is
  ordered before the answer). Q3 the steal timer (default: he takes the left option). Q5 Kirill's Drive folder.
- The team name, for the zip `TeamName_GameName.zip`.

## Known defects of the K1 build

- The debug lines (F5, F6, camera keys) are on screen in Shipping.
- An explosive shuriken looks like a plain one in the Publisher's hands; at the wall it punishes a player who
  cannot see why (finding of T-033).
- No sound, no music, no art beyond capsules. The fight length is measured with the bot only.

## Next steps, in the order of the plan

1. T-018: only the top-down camera stays.
2. T-019 Parry, then T-020 Ultimate, then T-021 (five mechanics, thresholds 80/60/40 and the FINAL NOTE at 20) and
   T-022 (the finisher with the Ultimate). Test first.
3. T-023 and T-024: the cosmetic layers on stand-ins. "Never cut": the way from the full game down to the bean,
   at least four layers.
4. Package Shipping, smoke, push to itch as soon as the address is known.
5. Blocks F and G on Saturday as far as the freeze allows.

Not a decision, a proposal for the author: with a day lost, the cut line of section 3 of `JAM_PLAN.md` comes into
play. Items 3 and 4 (the boss using stolen Parry and Ultimate, then mechanics 4 and 5 as such) are the ones that
would buy time for the cosmetic layers and the art, which are on the "never cut" list.

## Notes for Parry (T-019), read from the code, nothing written yet

- Add `EJamMechanic::Parry`, `JamSim::MechanicCount = 4`, the ledger initialiser, `JamLoadoutRules::Name`.
  `Owned` and `FirstOwned` are loops and need nothing.
- `FJamIntent::bParry` (key Q), a parry state on `FJamFighter` (active until, ready), pure `JamParryRules`.
- The hook is `AdvanceProjectiles` in `JamFightRules.cpp`: a projectile that would hit a parrying target changes
  its owner and flies back at the former one with a renewed life, with a new event for the view.
- New balance lines (window, cooldown, return speed and damage), the boss versions through
  `JamLoadoutRules::InHandsOf`. Every new field needs its line in `[JamBalance]` and in `JamTest::Balance()`.
- With four mechanics the third steal takes the two that are left; `JamStealRules` already allows it. The bot run
  test assumes `StealOrders = 6` and has to be recounted, and the steal and loadout tests that assume three
  mechanics need a look.

## Working notes that cost time to find

- Names in anonymous namespaces must be unique across the module: the build is a unity build.
- Do not build while a package cook or a clip recording runs: they use the editor binaries.
- `bash Tools/Build/demo_clip.sh [seconds] [output.mp4] [camera]` records a bot clip (3 to 4 minutes of wall time).
  The packaged exe takes `-JamDemo -JamCapture=<folder> -JamDemoSeconds=<n> -JamDemoCamera=<0|1|2>` too.
- After a full green run: `python Tools/Quality/check_code.py --tests-log Saved/BuildCycle/AutoTests_last.log
  --update-baseline`. The baseline is at 107 tests.
- The bot table is printed by `Jam.Bot.FightLengthIsInRange` into `Saved/BuildCycle/AutoTests_last.log` (lines
  with `bot table`).
- Shell: `rtk` shortens long grep output, `rtk proxy grep` prints it whole. Multi-line commit messages go through
  `git commit -F <file>`. No heredocs.
- Helper scripts of this session (not in the repo):
  `F:\Temp\Pavlo\claude\F--Unreal-Engine-UnrealProjects-CastleFight\c97397be-cf72-4ec9-ba97-3ec9a5e0a8bf\scratchpad\`
  with `bot_build.sh` (build and the bot table), `try_balance.sh`, `pkg_demo.sh` (run the packaged exe with the
  bot), `k1_clips.sh` (smoke and one clip per camera).
- Another session keeps a CastleFight editor open on this PC. Leave it alone.

## Prompt for the next session

```
Read F:\Unreal_Engine\UnrealProjects\MegaJam2026\HANDOFF.md, then JAM_START_PROMPT.md (sections "If the session
runs from another folder", "Who is where" is outdated: I am at the home PC, and "Standing rules"), CLAUDE.md and
.claude/rules/cpp.md of that project. Add this session to Tools/Devlog/sessions.json if it does not run from the
jam folder.

Check the clock first and tell me in three lines what fits before the feature freeze (Sat 22:00 PC clock) and
what you would cut by section 3 of JAM_PLAN.md. Wait for my answer on the cuts only; everything else goes on.

Camera is decided: 0, top-down. Then work in this order, test first, one commit per ticket: T-018 (only the
top-down camera stays), T-019 Parry, T-020 Ultimate, T-021 and T-022, then the cosmetic layers T-023 and T-024.
After each ticket: build and tests, commit, a short clip, three lines to me and to DEVLOG.md. Package Shipping
when block D is green, warn me before any game window, and push to itch once I give the page address.

# T-028 Music and sounds from Kirill (part: stub sound effects)

**Block:** G · **Status:** doing (sound effects on stubs done; Kirill's files and the Figma UI still open, Q5)

## Goal

Every action the player has to hear makes a sound: the twelve sounds of section 4 of `JAM_PLAN.md` plus the slam.
Stubs now, Kirill's files later under the same names, with no code change.

## Scope (this part)

- `JamSoundRules` (`Audio`, pure): `CuesOf(Events, Fight)` picks the cues of a frame's events, each cue once per
  frame in the order of first appearance. The katana (both sides), a shuriken throw (not memos, not the ball), an
  explosion, the slam, a dash, a deflection (the parry), the Ultimate slash, a hit on the boss, the hero hurt, the card
  opening, a mechanic taken, the stun giving everything back, and the winning slash as the final blow.
- `NameOf(Cue)`: `sfx_<what>_01`, the naming of Kirill's delivery.
- `AJamSounds` (`Audio`): one `USoundWave` per cue from `/Game/Audio/Sfx`, played 2D; the game mode calls it after
  the views.
- Stub sounds made in the jam by `Tools/Audio/make_stub_sfx.py` (synthesised, no samples), WAVs in `Audio/Stub/Sfx`,
  imported by `bash Tools/Audio/import_music.sh <root>/Tools/Audio/import_sfx.json`.

## Test seam

`Jam.Sound.EveryActionIsHeard`, `OnlyTheShurikenIsThrownAloud`, `ACueSoundsOncePerFrame`,
`TheFinalBlowHasItsOwnSound`, `NamesFollowTheDelivery`. Red first: 5 failing with stub rules.

## Done (this part)

139 `Jam.` tests green, 0 code check warnings. In game, `au.Debug.Sounds 1` lists `sfx_boss_hit_01` and
`sfx_shuriken_throw_01` beside the five music tracks: `Clips/t028_active_sounds.png`, 15 s `Clips/t028_sfx_debug.mp4`
(frames only, no sound track).

## Replacing the stubs

Put Kirill's WAVs into `Audio/Kirill/Sfx/` under the same names, copy `Tools/Audio/import_sfx.json` with those paths,
run the import script with it. No code change.

"""Creates an empty map asset. Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/create_empty_map.py"

The arena is spawned by the game mode at runtime, so the map only has to exist. An existing map is left alone.
"""
import unreal

FOLDER = "/Game/Maps"
NAME = "Arena"
PATH = "%s/%s" % (FOLDER, NAME)

if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(PATH):
    unreal.log("create_empty_map: %s already exists" % PATH)
else:
    world = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(NAME, FOLDER, unreal.World, unreal.WorldFactory())
    saved = world is not None and unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(PATH, only_if_is_dirty=False)
    unreal.log("create_empty_map: %s saved=%s" % (PATH, saved))

"""Creates the neon material of the stand-ins (T-027). Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/create_neon_material.py"

M_JamNeon is unlit: its colour is all emission, Color times Glow, so a Glow above 1 blooms. An existing material is
left alone.
"""
import unreal

FOLDER = "/Game/Materials"
NAME = "M_JamNeon"
PATH = "%s/%s" % (FOLDER, NAME)

if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(PATH):
    unreal.log("create_neon_material: %s already exists" % PATH)
else:
    lib = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
    mat = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(NAME, FOLDER, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    mat.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
    color = lib.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, -600, 0)
    color.set_editor_property("parameter_name", "Color")
    color.set_editor_property("default_value", unreal.LinearColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0))
    glow = lib.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, -600, 250)
    glow.set_editor_property("parameter_name", "Glow")
    glow.set_editor_property("default_value", 1.0)
    times = lib.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, -300, 100)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(color, "", times, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(glow, "", times, "B")
    lib.connect_material_property(times, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    saved = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(PATH, only_if_is_dirty=False)
    unreal.log("create_neon_material: %s saved=%s" % (PATH, saved))

# T-027 The neon arena and VFX on stand-ins

**Block:** F · **Status:** done on stand-ins (real models and VFX wait for the art, T-025, T-026)

## Goal

The full look has to be worth losing: a neon arena that blooms, so the drop to the engine grid at the second cut
reads as a loss.

## Scope

- `M_JamNeon` (`/Game/Materials`): unlit, all emission, `Color` times `Glow`; made by
  `Tools/Editor/create_neon_material.py` (headless pythonscript commandlet). `JamShapes::Glow` paints with it.
- Arena: posts, floor lines and a new neon band along the edge glow; the lines pulse on every beat of the 120 BPM
  music. The second cut still puts the grid on everything and hides lines and the edge.
- Effects (blades, flashes, warnings, sparks, rings) and projectiles glow; memos stay paper (glow 1).
- `JamNeonRules` (`View`, pure), numbers in `[JamNeon]`: `LineGlow(MusicTime)` (a kick on each beat, an exponential
  fall, never below the base), `Bloom(Layers)` (the camera blooms with the effects layer; the first cut takes the
  bloom with the effects).

## Test seam

`Jam.Neon.LinesPulseOnTheBeat`, `Jam.Neon.BloomGoesWithTheEffects`, `Jam.Neon.IniIsComplete`. Red first: 3 failing
with stub rules; on the way green the beat test caught a rounding epsilon in the code that dimmed the beat.

## Done

142 `Jam.` tests green, 0 code check warnings. Clip `Clips/t027_neon_arena.mp4` (30 s, bot). After the clip the posts
and edge were toned down in the ini (`PostGlow` 4 to 2.5, `EdgeGlow` 6 to 4): at 4 the posts washed out to pastel.

# Tickets

One file per ticket. Status: `todo`, `doing`, `done`, `cut`. A ticket is done when its `Jam.` tests are green in
`build_and_test.sh` and the change is committed.

## Architecture in five lines (decided at the start of block A)

- The fight is a **pure simulation**: `FJamFight` (plain data: two fighters, projectiles, hazards, the mechanic
  ledger, the steal state) advanced by `JamFightRules::Step` at a fixed 60 Hz. No world, no actors, flat arena in 2D.
- Everything a fighter does comes in as an **intent** (`FJamIntent`: move, aim, buttons). The player controller, the
  boss brain and the hero bot all write intents, so the hero and the boss run the same mechanic code.
- A **mechanic** is a sim-side component with an owner; a steal is a change of owner in the ledger.
- Folders: `Core` (types, balance, ini loading), `Sim` (rules and the subsystem that hosts the fight), `Game` (glue:
  game mode, controller, demo run), `View` (arena, fighters, projectiles, cameras), `UI`. `Core` and `Sim` never
  include `View`, `UI`, `Audio`. The game mode owns the frame order: input, simulation, views, camera.
- Balance numbers live in one place: `[JamBalance]` in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Packages the jam project for Win64 into Saved/Packaged/Windows and zips it next to the folder.
#   package.sh [--config Development|Shipping] [--name ZipBaseName] [--no-zip]
# Builds from the working tree. The editor can stay open: only the game target is compiled.
# The submission zip must be named TeamName_GameName: pass it with --name.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
OUT="$ROOT/Saved/Packaged"
LOG="$ROOT/Saved/BuildCycle/package_$(date +%H%M%S).log"
CONFIG=Development
NAME=""
DO_ZIP=1
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
	case "$1" in
		--config) shift; CONFIG="$1" ;;
		--name) shift; NAME="$1" ;;
		--no-zip) DO_ZIP=0 ;;
	esac
	shift
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts the packaged game for some seconds and reports what its log says.
#   smoke_package.sh [seconds] [map path, e.g. /Game/Maps/L_Main]
# Without a map the game opens its default map. A Shipping build writes no log unless it was built with logging:
# then only "still running" or "exited by itself" is reported.
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
SECONDS_TO_RUN="${1:-30}"
MAP="${2:-}"
GAME="$ROOT/Saved/Packaged/Windows"
EXE="$GAME/JamGame/Binaries/Win64/JamGame.exe"
LOG="$GAME/JamGame/Saved/Logs/JamGame.log"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pushes a packaged folder to the itch page pavyny/neon-ronin, channel windows. Key from .env, never printed.
#   itch_push.sh <folder> <version>     e.g. itch_push.sh Saved/Packaged/Windows block-d
# Needs butler in ~/bin (v15.32.0 installed Sat 14 Nov). Pipe the output through a filter before showing it.
set -euo pipefail
cd /f/Unreal_Engine/UnrealProjects/MegaJam2026
BUTLER_API_KEY="$(grep '^BUTLER_API_KEY=' .env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r"')"
export BUTLER_API_KEY
~/bin/butler.exe push "$1" pavyny/neon-ronin:windows --userversion "$2"
~/bin/butler.exe status pavyny/neon-ronin

# Session hand-off

Written Sat 14 Nov about 03:20 PC clock (UTC+2) at the end of the third jam session (autonomous, 02:24 to 05:24).
The next session starts from the prompt at the bottom of this file. Earlier hand-offs are in git history (`7422eca`,
`b5cb811`). The report of this session: `Reports/session3_report.md`.

## Where we are

- **Last commit:** the hand-off commit after `50ffc23` (T-031). Working tree clean except `Art/Cover/` (the author's
  cover draft, not ours to commit without a word).
- **Clock:** feature freeze Sat 22:00, video Sun 18:00, submit Sun 20:00 and never later than 21:59.
- **This session:** T-029, T-028 (sound effects part), T-027, T-031 committed, one commit per ticket, a clip each.
- **itch:** PUSH_LINE
- **Package:** PACKAGE_LINE

## What the game does today (143 `Jam.` tests green, code check without warnings)

- Top-down camera only. Five mechanics: katana (LMB), shuriken (RMB), dash (Space), parry (Q), Ultimate (E).
- Four cuts at 80, 60, 40 percent (a pair on a card) and the FINAL NOTE at 20. Each cut strips a cosmetic layer
  and a music stem. At zero: stun, everything returns, only the Ultimate wins.
- Neon look on stand-ins (T-027): an unlit emissive material `M_JamNeon`, glowing posts, edge band and floor lines
  that pulse on the beat, glowing effects and shots, bloom that goes with the effects layer.
- Readability (T-029): sparks on hits, camera shake on heavy blows, the boss flashes by the size of the blow, the
  parry ring closes with its window, his explosive shuriken is yellow, pulses and drags its blast circle.
- Sound effects (T-028 part): 13 synthesised stubs under Kirill's names, picked from the step events.
- Balance (T-031): Publisher health 4800. Bot 60 of 60, median 142 s (left 153, right 151, mixed 141).

## Open with people (`QUESTIONS.md`)

- Q8 the sound list for Kirill (13 names, the slam is extra), Q9 the longer fight (4800 health).
- Still open: Q7 the cuts, Q1 the name, Q2 the concepts, Q3 the steal timer, Q5 Kirill's Drive folder, the team name
  for `TeamName_GameName.zip`.

## Known defects and gaps

- No real art: models (T-025, T-026) need the author's Meshy or Tripo work and Q2. The neon is on stand-ins.
- No music or sounds from Kirill yet: stubs only. The clips have no sound track (frames only).
- A person's fight is not measured; the bot's median is 142 s.
- `Jam.Bot.SlashesWhenTheBossIsInReach` was written together with its code, never seen red.
- The blast ring of his explosive shuriken was not checked on a frame yet (CLIP_LINE).

## Remaining tickets, suggested order

1. **T-028 rest**: Kirill's music and sounds (needs Q5), UI from his Figma designs.
2. **T-025, T-026 art**: hero and boss models with the author; the neon material is ready for their emissive parts.
3. **A person's playtest** of the 4800 balance (author or Evgeny), then T-031 numbers by hand if needed.
4. **T-032 submission** on Sunday: itch page, `THIRD_PARTY.md`, tool list, dev log, release candidate zip.

## Working notes that cost time to find

- `AActor` already has a member `Layers`: do not name a member that in an actor.
- A clip (`Tools/Build/demo_clip.sh <seconds> <out.mp4>`) takes about 5 s of wall time per second of clip; the
  cook can run at the same time, a build cannot. The clip has no sound: frames only.
- `au.Debug.Sounds 1` through `-ExecCmds` shows the active sounds on a captured frame: the audio evidence (run the
  editor binary with `-game -JamDemo -JamCapture=<dir>` like `demo_clip.sh` does).
- The ImportAssets commandlet exits 1 with "Invalid Destination Path ()" after a good import: expected. It loads the
  last built game DLL: build first, or its constructors log stale paths.
- Materials are made headless: `UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script=<abs path>`
  (`Tools/Editor/create_neon_material.py`).
- `JamShapes::Paint` and `JamShapes::Glow` each keep their own material instance; a pooled shape that switches
  between them makes a new instance each time, so keep one pool on one of them.
- Unity build: names in anonymous namespaces must be unique across the module.
- Multi-line commit messages through `git commit -F <file>`, no heredocs (a hook blocks them).

## Prompt for the next session

```
Read F:\Unreal_Engine\UnrealProjects\MegaJam2026\HANDOFF.md, then CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/cpp.md, QUESTIONS.md,
Reports/session3_report.md and the "Standing rules" of JAM_START_PROMPT.md.

Check the clock first and say how long it is to the feature freeze (Sat 22:00 PC clock). Then ask me which of the
"Remaining tickets" of HANDOFF.md we take, and whether I have answers to Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9. Test first, one
commit per ticket, build and tests, a short clip and a DEVLOG.md entry after each. Never cross the feature freeze.
```

# Session hand-off

Written Sat 14 Nov about 03:20 PC clock (UTC+2) at the end of the third jam session (autonomous, 02:24 to 05:24).
The next session starts from the prompt at the bottom of this file. Earlier hand-offs are in git history (`7422eca`,
`b5cb811`). The report of this session: `Reports/session3_report.md`.

## Where we are

- **Last commit:** the hand-off commit after `50ffc23` (T-031). Working tree clean except `Art/Cover/` (the author's
  cover draft, not ours to commit without a word).
- **Clock:** feature freeze Sat 22:00, video Sun 18:00, submit Sun 20:00 and never later than 21:59.
- **This session:** T-029, T-028 (sound effects part), T-027, T-031 committed, one commit per ticket, a clip each.
- **itch:** pushed 02:55 to `pavyny/neon-ronin`, channel `windows`, version `session-3`, build #2380360 (patch 131 MB from #2380090), status processing at push.
- **Package:** Shipping `Saved/Packaged/Windows/JamGame.exe` (599 MB folder), zip `Saved/Packaged/NeonRonin_Session3.zip` (305 MB), packaged 02:53; the cook compiled `M_JamNeon`.

## What the game does today (143 `Jam.` tests green, code check without warnings)

- Top-down camera only. Five mechanics: katana (LMB), shuriken (RMB), dash (Space), parry (Q), Ultimate (E).
- Four cuts at 80, 60, 40 percent (a pair on a card) and the FINAL NOTE at 20. Each cut strips a cosmetic layer
  and a music stem. At zero: stun, everything returns, only the Ultimate wins.
- Neon look on stand-ins (T-027): an unlit emissive material `M_JamNeon`, glowing posts, edge band and floor lines
  that pulse on the beat, glowing effects and shots, bloom that goes with the effects layer.
- Readability (T-029): sparks on hits, camera shake on heavy blows, the boss flashes by the size of the blow, the
  parry ring closes with its window, his explosive shuriken is yellow, pulses and drags its blast circle.
- Sound effects (T-028 part): 13 synthesised stubs under Kirill's names, picked from the step events.
- Balance (T-031): Publisher health 4800. Bot 60 of 60, median 142 s (left 153, right 151, mixed 141).

## Open with people (`QUESTIONS.md`)

- Q8 the sound list for Kirill (13 names, the slam is extra), Q9 the longer fight (4800 health).
- Still open: Q7 the cuts, Q1 the name, Q2 the concepts, Q3 the steal timer, Q5 Kirill's Drive folder, the team name
  for `TeamName_GameName.zip`.

## Known defects and gaps

- No real art: models (T-025, T-026) need the author's Meshy or Tripo work and Q2. The neon is on stand-ins.
- No music or sounds from Kirill yet: stubs only. The clips have no sound track (frames only).
- A person's fight is not measured; the bot's median is 142 s.
- `Jam.Bot.SlashesWhenTheBossIsInReach` was written together with its code, never seen red.
- The sounds of the package are unheard: nobody has played the session 3 build with sound on.

## Remaining tickets, suggested order

1. **T-028 rest**: Kirill's music and sounds (needs Q5), UI from his Figma designs.
2. **T-025, T-026 art**: hero and boss models with the author; the neon material is ready for their emissive parts.
3. **A person's playtest** of the 4800 balance (author or Evgeny), then T-031 numbers by hand if needed.
4. **T-032 submission** on Sunday: itch page, `THIRD_PARTY.md`, tool list, dev log, release candidate zip.

## Working notes that cost time to find

- `AActor` already has a member `Layers`: do not name a member that in an actor.
- A clip (`Tools/Build/demo_clip.sh <seconds> <out.mp4>`) takes about 5 s of wall time per second of clip; the
  cook can run at the same time, a build cannot. The clip has no sound: frames only.
- `au.Debug.Sounds 1` through `-ExecCmds` shows the active sounds on a captured frame: the audio evidence (run the
  editor binary with `-game -JamDemo -JamCapture=<dir>` like `demo_clip.sh` does).
- The ImportAssets commandlet exits 1 with "Invalid Destination Path ()" after a good import: expected. It loads the
  last built game DLL: build first, or its constructors log stale paths.
- Materials are made headless: `UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script=<abs path>`
  (`Tools/Editor/create_neon_material.py`).
- `JamShapes::Paint` and `JamShapes::Glow` each keep their own material instance; a pooled shape that switches
  between them makes a new instance each time, so keep one pool on one of them.
- Unity build: names in anonymous namespaces must be unique across the module.
- Multi-line commit messages through `git commit -F <file>`, no heredocs (a hook blocks them).

Read F:\Unreal_Engine\UnrealProjects\MegaJam2026\HANDOFF.md, then CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/cpp.md, QUESTIONS.md,
Reports/session3_report.md and the "Standing rules" of JAM_START_PROMPT.md.

Check the clock first and say how long it is to the feature freeze (Sat 22:00 PC clock). Then ask me which of the
"Remaining tickets" of HANDOFF.md we take, and whether I have answers to Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9. Test first, one
commit per ticket, build and tests, a short clip and a DEVLOG.md entry after each. Never cross the feature freeze.
```

# Questions for the author

Things that need Pavlo's eyes. The work does not wait: each question has the default the agent already took.

## Open

### Q1. The name NEON RONIN is taken on Steam (Thu 13:38)

- Checked: Steam app 1929540 is "Neon Ronin" by TYPE-III, a turn-based cyberpunk rogue-lite, status "coming soon"
  (store page read on 12 Nov). An itch search for "neon ronin" showed no game with this exact name.
- A jam entry with the same name is not forbidden, but the win title is the name, and a search for the game will
  land on theirs.
- **Default:** keep NEON RONIN as the working title today; all strings are in one place, a rename is one line.
- Options if you want a free name: NEON RONIN ZERO, LAST RONIN OF NEON, RONIN.EXE, NEON BUSHIDO. Not checked yet;
  say which ones you like and they get checked.

### Q2. Concept round 1: which hero and which boss? (Thu 13:39)

- Files `Art/Concepts/r1_*.png`, sent to the chat. Hero A (lean, black with cyan and magenta piping) or hero B
  (kasa hat, indigo coat). Boss A (charcoal suit, kabuto, gold armour) or boss B (white suit, gold, sunglasses).
- **Default:** hero A and boss A: they match the lineup image and both arena paintings. No model is ordered before
  your answer; hero animations wait for the camera choice anyway.

### Q3. What happens when the steal timer runs out? (Thu 13:40)

- The plan says the fight slows for 3 seconds and the player picks. It does not say what happens without a pick.
- **Default:** the Publisher takes the left option.
- Alternative: he takes a random one, or the slowdown lasts until the player picks.

### Q7. The cut line: what goes by section 3 of JAM_PLAN.md (Sat 00:49)

- Proposed: cut item 1 (intro), item 2 (DLSS), item 3 (the Publisher uses a stolen Parry or Ultimate: he only takes
  them), item 5 (cameras, done by T-018). Item 4 (mechanics 4 and 5) was conditional and is not needed: both are in.
- **Default taken:** the Publisher only takes Parry and Ultimate. No answer yet.

### Q8. The sound list for Kirill: thirteen names, one more than the plan (Sat 02:55)

- T-028 plays stub sounds under these names: `sfx_katana_slash_01`, `sfx_shuriken_throw_01`, `sfx_explosion_01`,
  `sfx_slam_01`, `sfx_dash_01`, `sfx_parry_01`, `sfx_ultimate_01`, `sfx_boss_hit_01`, `sfx_hero_hurt_01`,
  `sfx_steal_card_01`, `sfx_steal_01`, `sfx_everything_back_01`, `sfx_final_blow_01` (WAV, 48 kHz).
- **Defaults taken:** the slam got its own sound (not in section 4 of the plan); the ball shot and the memo volley
  are silent; the parry sounds only when it deflects, not when Q opens the window. Kirill's files under these names
  replace the stubs with no code change (`Tickets/T-028_sound_effects.md`).

### Q9. A longer fight: the Publisher has 4800 health, was 4000 (Sat 02:55)

- The bot's median sat at 122 s, 2 s over the test floor. T-031 raised his health: bot median 142 s, all 60 fights and
  all 20 steal orders still won. A person's fight is longer than the bot's and is not measured.
- **Default taken:** 4800. If your hands say it drags, one line in `[JamBalance]` takes it back.

### Q5. The Google Drive folder from Kirill

- Needed to check reading one WAV. Not blocking today: the prototype has no sound.

## Answered

### Q4. The itch draft page address

- **Answer (Sat 14 Nov, in chat):** https://pavyny.itch.io/neon-ronin, channel `windows`. butler v15.32.0 installed in
  `~/bin`. The first push was blocked by an unverified itch email (Q4b); the author verified it on Sat 14 Nov 02:15
  and the block D build was pushed (`Tools/Build/itch_push.sh`).

### Q6. Which camera? Answer by Friday 07:00 (Thu 14:10)

- Clip `Clips/block_a.mp4`, sent to the chat: 8 seconds on each camera with a bot playing. In the build: F1, F2, F3.
- The clip shows the look only. The feel of the aim (cursor against mouse look) needs your hands on the 23:00 build.
- Thu 16:05: one 50 second clip per camera, sent to the chat: `Clips/k1_cam0_topdown.mp4`,

(Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. I played three fights of the session-3 itch build. My feedback, most important first:

1. Controls feel sluggish. Aiming is hard. I want a visible cursor and the hero turning to it instantly, with no lag or smoothing, like Hades 2.
2. Parry is not discoverable. The player only learns that enemy projectiles can be deflected back at the boss when the Publisher steals Parry. It has to be obvious before that.
3. Parry looks like a melee attack, while the melee attacks themselves have no animation. After Parry is stolen I can still hit in melee, but with no visible swing, so it reads as a bug.
4. I never found the Ultimate in three fights. One line of HUD text "E ULTIMATE 64%" is easy to miss. Same problem as Parry: a mechanic the player does not know about until it is gone.

Before any code: use AskUserQuestion to ask me, interactively, every open question you have. That covers how to fix the four points above (show me options with your recommendation first) and the open ones in QUESTIONS.md: Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9 and the team name. @RTK.md

# Рабочий флоу по умолчанию

Структурированный флоу — это: обсуждение → грил (/grilling) → тикеты → реализация через TDD (/tdd, красный-зелёный на согласованных швах).

Перед стартом каждой НОВОЙ задачи (не подзадачи текущей) реши, нужен ли он:

- **Уверен, что флоу не нужен** — скипай молча, не спрашивая, и сразу берись за работу. Это про мелкие правки, однострочники, операционные и разведочные действия, ответы на вопросы, правку конфигов и доков.
- **Уверен, что нужен, или сомневаешься** — спроси одним коротким вопросом, каким именно флоу вести (полный / только обсуждение + грил / без флоу). Задал вопрос — жди ответа, не начинай работу до него.

Для чисто исследовательских и операционных задач без производственного кода (разведка API, генерация контента, публикация) в вопросе сразу отметь, что TDD-часть там применить не к чему — уместны только обсуждение и грил.

# Бюджет лимитов: прогноз перед тяжёлым запуском

Перед любым запуском, который может съесть заметную часть 5-часового лимита, сначала
напиши в чат прогноз и жди моего явного «да». Тяжёлым считается: Workflow (любой),
больше 3 субагентов разом или в цикле, фоновые агенты на длинные задачи. Правило
действует всегда, в том числе в ultracode-сессиях: ultracode разрешает workflow, но не
отменяет прогноз и подтверждение.

В прогнозе:
- сколько агентов (с учётом верификаторов и циклов, худший случай);
- грубая оценка токенов (ориентир: агент-исследователь 50-150k, Opus дороже Sonnet);
- примерная доля 5-часового лимита и время;
- дешёвый вариант (меньше агентов, Sonnet или Haiku, без верификации) рядом с полным.

Хук `workflow-guard` на каждый Workflow запрашивает моё подтверждение, но прогноз
в чате должен прийти до вызова, а не вместо него. Если запуск уже идёт и расход
растёт быстрее прогноза, остановись и скажи.

# Стиль письма

**Длинные тире.** По умолчанию ставь запятую, двоеточие или скобки там, где
напрашивается «—». Тире оставляй для настоящего разрыва мысли, и не чаще одного
раза на длинный текст. Правило касается всего, что пишешь ты: ответы в терминале,
комментарии к PR и ревью, сообщения коммитов, документация, отчёты. Мой
собственный текст не переписывай, если об этом не просили.

**Язык в коде, коммитах и пул-реквестах.** Комментарии в коде, сообщения коммитов
(git и dv), комментарии, ревью и описания PR всегда по-английски, даже если
окружающий код прокомментирован по-русски или коллега в треде пишет по-русски.
Старые русские комментарии не переводи, если об этом не просили. Разговор со мной
в терминале, наоборот, по-русски.


# Shell и деструктивные операции

- **Никаких heredoc и многострочных строк с backslash-экранированием в Bash.** Всё
  многострочное (скрипты, JSON, тексты) пишется в файл через Write, потом файл
  исполняется или читается. Хук `bash-guard` блокирует heredoc автоматически.
- **Деструктивные операции** (rm -rf, drop, truncate, delete from, firestore delete,
  git clean и т.п.) только через скрипт-файл с флагом `--dry-run`, включённым по
  умолчанию. Сначала прогон в dry-run с точными счётчиками, потом остановка и
  ожидание моего явного «да». Хук переводит такие команды в режим подтверждения.
